# FM3: Unpaid Work

**Display ID:** FM3  
**Pillar:** Financial Criteria  
**Points:** 1  
**Mandatory for Certification:** Yes  
**Category:** Basis of Financial Sustainability  
**Applicability:** Project, Designing Entity  
**Project types:** Print, Digital, Hybrid  
**Related SDGs:** SDG 1, SDG 5, SDG 8, SDG 10

## Summary
Compensates all designers.

## Description
The design entity and the project did not request unpaid work, also known as "free pitching", "speculative work", or "spec work", from designers, including interns and student designers.

## Why it matters
All design work is financially compensated.

## Extended guidance
## What is “spec work” (also knowns as “speculative work” and “free pitching”)?
Unpaid work, also known as “spec work” refers to speculative work, meaning working without compensation on a project, in a tender process or competition, for example. Ico-D, the International Council of Design, explains "Spec work is providing unpaid work in the hopes to obtain a paid contract. Though this practice is common in some industries it is considered unethical in design. Spec work diminishes the value of design services and it encourages poor practice.

For more details, see their [Professional Code of Conduct](https://www.theicod.org/resources/professional-code-of-conduct).
